best_for: Paying Proton Mail users who want to keep working in Outlook, Thunderbird or Apple Mail without giving up encryption.

points.title: Your mail client talks to a local server
points.text: Bridge runs a small IMAP and SMTP server on your computer and handles the encryption. Your mail client connects to it like any other account, so mail you download stays readable offline.

points.title: Paid plans only
points.text: Proton says Bridge works only with a paid plan that includes Proton Mail, such as Mail Plus or Proton Unlimited. A free account cannot use it.

points.title: Keep it running
points.text: Your client syncs only while Bridge is running, which is why it starts with the computer by default and keeps running in the background after you close its window.

points.title: Tested clients
points.text: Proton tests Thunderbird on every system, Outlook 2010 to 2021 on Windows, and Apple Mail, Outlook 2011 to 2019 and new Outlook on macOS. On Linux only Thunderbird is tested. Other clients may work, but Proton warns of possible crashes and limited support.

points.title: Linux needs a keychain
points.text: Bridge stores its secrets in the system keychain. On Linux that means the Secret Service API, such as GNOME Keyring, or `pass`. The project README says only GNOME Keyring works without major problems today.

points.title: Open source, with its own password
points.text: The source is on GitHub under GPL-3.0. Bridge gives you a separate password for your mail client, which never leaves your computer, and it updates itself through a signed launcher.

points.title: Platform notes
points.text: The Windows installer is x64 only and installs for the whole machine. macOS gets one universal build. The Flathub build is x64 only and not marked verified. The Windows listing keeps 27 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
